survey: A sci-fi control console in a simple desk shape, seen from the front-right at three-quarter view. The main body is a rounded light-grey box resting flat on a riveted metal floor; its base touches the floor along its full length and casts a contact shadow. The top is a sloped dark-grey control panel, angled toward the operator, framed by the body walls. The right side wall's top edge follows the same slope. A raised grey rail runs along the high back edge of the panel and sits on top of the back wall. On the panel: two round dial gauges (white with a red needle, green with a dark needle), each set in a raised bezel; eight round push buttons in two staggered rows (yellow and red), each in its own grey collar, flush to the panel and easy to press; and on the right a dark lever housing with a slot. A metal lever stem with a red ball knob rises from a collar at the bottom end of the slot, so it can slide along the track. The front face holds one recessed drawer panel with a single grey pull handle, centred and reachable. Every part sits on or in a surface that supports it. Nothing floats, there are no loose cables, and the counts are plausible for a simplified console.
